judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause makes a delinquent Employer liable for "any expenses incurred in effectuating such payment," with a non-exhaustive list ending in "interest at a rate of 18 percent per annum" — the general phrase plus the odd inclusion of interest as an "expense" invites argument about whether 18% is a fixed rate, a ceiling, or displaced by ERISA's statutory interest. The catch-all "including, but not limited to" against enumerated specifics leaves the reach of recoverable amounts genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.4(a) refers to interest "at a rate calculated in accordance with Section 9.5" and 9.7(b)-(c) computes both interest and the 20% liquidated damages "in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5," yet 9.5(b) states a flat rate rather than a method, and Amendment No. 2 later adds "or such other interest rate that the Trustees deem appropriate," creating tension over which rate governs a given delinquency. The interaction of 9.5(b), 9.4(b), 9.7 and Amendment No. 2 is a live source of internal inconsistency.
judgments.clause_name: Section 9.5(b) — Default in Payment (18 percent interest)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Preamble identifies the parties and named Trustees in definite terms; the only oddities are typographical ("tnion," "as of the September 1, 1993") which do not change meaning. It equates "Fund" and "Plan" as labels, a loose usage but one clarified by Article 1 definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.20 defines "Plan" as the rules and regulations while 1.22 defines "Fund" as the corpus, so the Preamble's "(the 'Fund' or 'Plan')" is slightly loose, but the definitions article expressly governs. Amendment No. 4 replaces the Preamble, keeping it current and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain recital of fact with a defined term; no vague operative language. Nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.8's definition and Article 9's contribution mechanics; no operative provision points the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple background recital; the typo "contenplate" is immaterial to meaning. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 3's appointment scheme by Association and Union.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Exclusive purpose of providing pension and retirement benefits" is a standard formulation; "certain employees" is qualified by the defined term Covered Employees. Wording is definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1(a) permits "such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine," which is broader than the recital's "pension and retirement benefits" — a mild recital-versus-operative divergence, though Section 2.2 harmonises with "related benefits."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely historical recital with definite dates; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2 and Article 10's amendment power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite recital of an amendment power, though it cites "Paragraph 18" of a superseded instrument. The cross-reference is to the prior document, not this one, so no internal defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The restated Agreement's amendment power sits in Section 10.1, not Paragraph 18, so a reader could question whether the recited authority matches — but the recital plainly refers to the pre-restatement trust agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate consideration language; "promises" is rendered "prom-ises" only by hyphenation. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the whole instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard definitional preamble with the usual "unless the context otherwise requires" carve-out, which is common and rarely litigated here. No specific ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7 imports Plan definitions "except as otherwise expressly provided herein," which sits comfortably with this introduction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Administrator as the Board or a duly authorized delegate; definite and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1's text is garbled ("Where the Administrator is a Trust Fund") but that defect lies in 7.1, not in this definition; 1.6 also names the Board as ERISA "administrator," which coheres.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition tied to a named instrument and date; no vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Preamble and Section 10.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Preamble, Section 10.3(a)(2) and Section 12.8(d) all use "Publishers' Association of New York City," so the definition is marginally off, though no one could seriously doubt the referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "both the Chairman and Secretary of the Board" could mean jointly or each individually, a genuine but minor ambiguity; the rest is layered but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 requires Chairman and Secretary jointly to execute documents and Section 12.6 makes the Chairman's certificate alone conclusive, so the joint/several question recurs across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such other person or entity who, as a result of his relationship to the Covered Employee, is entitled under the terms of the Plan" defers to the Plan, so the boundary is set elsewhere; the wording itself is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.5's assignment restrictions and Section 12.7's incorporation of Plan definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, tied to ERISA statutory definitions with citations. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.2 and 5.14 allocating overall control to the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition says "Internal Revenue Code of 1936," plainly a typographical error for 1986 — a mechanical mistake in a defined term that is relied on throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.3, 4.4, 10.1(b) and 10.2 all turn on "the Code," so the erroneous year propagates, though any court would correct it as an obvious scrivener's error.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "or other written agreement between an Employer and the Union, which is in force and effect and is acceptable to the Board" is a catch-all after enumerated types, and "acceptable to the Board" is an undefined standard of approval. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4(a) requires a Collective Bargaining Agreement "approved by the Board," while Section 9.1 makes contribution rates governed by the CBAs, so the Board-acceptance filter could be read differently across these provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in its main operation, with an express reconciliation clause ("to the extent that the provisions thereof are not inconsistent with the terms of this Agreement"). That proviso itself anticipates and resolves conflict.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5(h) authorises pooling into Collective Trusts and Section 5.7 imposes prudence duties; the exculpation here for Collective Trust trustees fits that framework.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear definition with a minimum composition requirement of one Trustee from each side.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tied to the CBA and contribution obligation; definite boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.13 and 9.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.12 speaks of appointing a bank or trust company as Corporate Trustee but excludes broker-dealers, whereas 1.12 includes broker-dealers as potential Corporate Trustees — a small inconsistency between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: employers required to contribute pursuant to a CBA. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Preamble's broader "such other employers which from time to time become contributing employers," and with Sections 2.4 and 9.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple cross-referencing definition; "successors and assigns" applied to individual trustees is loose but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.3(a), 3.7 and 3.9; Amendment No. 4 updates 3.3 without disturbing this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory definition; typographical noise only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to a specific ERISA section and regulation; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.5(p)'s ancillary trustee requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires "written communications signed by an Authorized Person" yet the parenthetical extends to telex and similar systems where signature is inferred from verification — a small tension between "signed" and the electronic carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(a) requires specimen signatures for those giving Instructions, which coheres with the signature requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A layered but precise definition keyed to ERISA and the Advisers Act; the requirements are enumerated conjunctively and clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.1-8.3 and the Board's power under 1.12 to appoint the Custodian in dual roles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 8.1(b)'s segregation requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite; identifies the Plan as the detailed rules adopted by the Board.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Preamble uses "Fund" and "Plan" interchangeably, which is looser than this definition, but Article 1 governs and Sections 4.2 and 5.2 use "Plan" consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list introduced by "including, but not limited to" and closed by catch-all subsection (k) — the classic general-versus-specific structure, though the opening words "all Trust Fund securities of any and every kind" make the breadth express.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.5's investment powers and Section 11.2's valuation provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite and comprehensive as to the corpus.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.1, 5.12 and 1.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.9, 3.10 and 3.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite; "and any affiliates thereof" is broad but the referent entity is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Preamble's identical formulation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple cross-referencing definition; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.3(b), 3.8 and 3.10, as amended by Amendment No. 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A naming provision; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Preamble and Section 9.3's payee designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "certain pension and related benefits" uses "related benefits" without definition, an open-ended category whose boundary is not fixed by the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1(a) similarly permits "such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine" while the Preamble recital speaks only of "pension and retirement benefits" — a possible recital-versus-operative gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deemed-amendment device ("this Agreement shall be deemed amended in such fashion as will implement the purposes of this Trust") is inherently open-ended: who determines the fashion, and what amendment results, is not specified. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 requires amendments by unanimous Board vote subject to conditions, and Section 10.2 forbids certain amendments, so an automatic deemed amendment sits uneasily with the prescribed amendment machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1 says nothing in the Trust Agreement shall change the terms of any CBA, which sits in some tension with an unconditional agreement to be bound to all amendments and Trustee decisions affecting contribution costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Numbered "3.2" in the OCR though it is Section 3.1; the substance — two Employer and three Union Trustees — is definite. The cross-reference to Section 3.4 for appointments is accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward acceptance language; definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of names; nothing to construe beyond identification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Names three Union Trustees consistent with Section 3.1 as originally drafted; superseded by Amendment No. 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "as soon as practicable" is a soft timing standard, but it governs only the delivery of copies and carries no consequence for delay.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.9, 3.10 and 3.11's designation mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: service until death, incapacity, resignation or removal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.6's deemed resignation when a designating Contributing Employer ceases adds a further terminating event not listed here, and Section 3.8 ties Union Trustee tenure to union office — mild incompleteness in 3.5's list.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1 and 3.3(a) provide that Employer Trustees are selected by the Association, not by individual Contributing Employers, and 3.9 provides for successors on any vacancy, so 3.6's deemed-resignation/no-replacement rule conflicts with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite removal mechanic with immediate effect on filing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.9's successor procedure; contrasts deliberately with 3.8's treatment of Union Trustees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Titled "Removal of Union Trustees" but the text mostly prescribes who the Union Trustees are and addresses removal only "by operation of law" — a mismatch between heading and content, and no mechanism for removal by the Union itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite mechanism keyed to a written certificate from the Association.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.1 and 3.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite vesting provision; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.4, 3.9 and 3.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.7's prudence and diversification duty and Section 7.2(5)'s retained fiduciary functions sit in tension with the Trustees being "forever released and discharged" as to transferred assets; Section 1.12's Corporate Trustee definition also includes broker-dealers not permitted here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine" is a catch-all following the specifics "pension, retirement" — the ejusdem generis boundary of "related benefits" is not fixed. The rest of the clause is carefully drafted protection language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Preamble recital limits the Fund to "pension and retirement benefits" and Section 10.2 bars diversion to any purpose other than "pension or related benefits," so the reach of 4.1(a)'s catch-all interacts with those limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: eligibility and benefit terms live in the Plan, which the Board may amend or terminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.2, 7.2(2) and 10.1; the unlimited power to terminate the Plan "at any time" sits against Section 10.3's termination formalities for the Trust, but those are distinct instruments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1(b) and 5.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite; vests receipt and title in the Board and permits deposit with Custodians.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(8) requires the Board to review, approve and pay expenses "of the type set forth in Sections 5.3 and 5.5(n)," which coheres; Section 5.3(d) bars Trustee compensation consistent with 5.3(a)(vii)'s reimbursement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully drafted; the insurance-company protections are stated in definite terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1(b), 4.3 and 5.3(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, with the bond amount tied to ERISA Section 412.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite; "need not be verbatim" is a clear limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite appointment and segregation mechanics; a typographical "Securities of other property" for "or other property" does not obscure meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.19, 8.4(b) and 5.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite; "periodically" in (c) is a soft frequency term but of little operative bite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.8 and 7.2(13)'s monitoring duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite; grants order-placement authority subject to the management agreement and ERISA.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (b)'s "liquidated damage penalty equal to the greater of interest on, or twenty percent of, the unpaid contributions" is elliptical (interest over what period?), and "penalty" alongside "liquidated damage" is internally awkward. The cross-reference to Section 9.5 for the interest rate is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.4(a) says collection costs "shall be paid from the Fund" and then, notwithstanding, allows recovery from the Employer, while 9.5(b) and 9.7(d) make the Employer liable for those costs — an allocation that requires harmonising.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite; defines "unpaid contributions" and identifies the ERISA enforcement sections. The OCR renders 502(g)(2) as "502(g) 2)" without changing meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.5, 9.7 and 9.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item (e) "such other legal or equitable relief as the court deems appropriate" is a catch-all after four specifics, but it merely tracks ERISA Section 502(g)(2) and defers to the court. Otherwise mechanical and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It computes interest "in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5," yet 9.5(b) states a flat 18% rate rather than a method, and Amendment No. 2 makes the rate discretionary — a cross-reference that no longer fits cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite anti-waiver saving clause; the Article is called "Article IX" here and "Article 9" elsewhere in the same sentence, a trivial inconsistency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.5(a) and 9.6's "in addition to any other remedies" framing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all records deemed necessary by such persons" gives the auditor's own judgment the boundary, and "The Board may charge an Employer for the cost of conducting an audit" states no condition or limit. Both are open-ended but plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.4(a) says collection costs are paid from the Fund, while 9.9 allows charging audit costs to the Employer — related but not squarely conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sweeping mandatory arbitration for "any and all claims by third parties (including Employers) ... concerning the assessment ... of withdrawal liability," with a definite forum and rules; the final sentence preserves the Fund's court action. "Third parties (including Employers)" is slightly odd since Employers are parties to the Trust arrangement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.2 chooses New York law subject to ERISA preemption and this clause says arbitrations are governed by New York law "to the extent not superceded by ERISA," which is consistent; Section 9.6's court-action right is expressly preserved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Condition (a) — the amendment must not be "inconsistent with the purposes for which the Fund was established" — imports Section 2.2's open "related benefits" purpose as a limit on amendment power, an inherently contestable standard. The rest is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Condition (c) barring "unequal voting power" between Employer and Union Trustees interacts with Section 3.1's 2-3 composition, reconciled only through Section 6.4's unit-voting; Section 10.2 adds a further limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite prohibition with a single express exception cross-referenced to Section 10.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4 permits returning mistaken or non-deductible contributions to an Employer, yet 10.2 excepts only Section 10.3 — a direct textual conflict between the two return-of-contribution provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three termination triggers stated definitely, with a clear exclusive-benefit constraint on distribution of surplus; "distribute or apply any remaining surplus in a manner consistent, in their opinion, with this Agreement" leaves the method to Board opinion but the constraint is express.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.2 excepts Section 10.3 from the no-diversion rule, yet 10.3(b) itself says no part of the corpus shall revert to any Employer — so the excepted provision creates no actual exception, an internal oddity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite recordkeeping duties with a clear inspection right and annual audit requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.1(g) and 11.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such commercially acceptable valuation method or methods determined by the Board" leaves the method to Board choice, a soft but conventional standard bounded by prudence and good faith.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.7 and 11.1(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the New York City metropolitan area" is a geographically imprecise boundary, and the clause then deems the Board "located at that address" though no address is stated in the section. Both are genuine looseness in short compass.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.8 supplies actual addresses in Long Island City and Section 12.5 designates the Board as process agent, so the practical location is fixed elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard New York choice-of-law clause with an express ERISA-preemption qualifier; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.10's New York law and venue provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.2's reference to signing "any counterpart or copy hereof."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite interpretive rules on headings, number and gender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Useful in reading Section 3.8's heading against its content, and otherwise consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence designating the Board as process agent; definite though it gives no address.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.1 deems the Board located at the principal office and 12.8 gives the address, filling the gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite third-party protection; the conclusive effect attaches specifically to instruments "executed by the Chairman of the Trustees."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 requires both Chairman and Secretary (or a resolution-authorised equal group) to execute documents on the Board's behalf, so 12.6's single-Chairman conclusiveness is in tension with the execution requirement.
judgments.clause_name: 12.6 Validity of Trustees' Accounts and Instruments

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite incorporation of Plan definitions with an express carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Potentially circular with Section 1.20's definition of Plan by reference to this Agreement, but Article 1's own definitions expressly govern where provided.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanical notice provision listing addresses; the excerpt is cut off mid-sentence on the deemed-receipt rule, and deeming notice given "when deposited by first-class mail" is definite if harsh. Nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Superseded in part by Amendment No. 1 and Amendment No. 3, which update addresses and rename the Fund Administrator as Fund Director — a naming drift against Section 1.1's "Administrator."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The excerpt begins mid-sentence ("uhé Board) or any person claiming by or through them"), so the class of persons denied any interest is not visible in the quoted text. The substance — no entitlement until the Board determines eligibility — is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1(a) and Section 5.2 obligate the Board to pay benefits per the Plan, and Section 5.14 makes Board determinations final, which together support rather than contradict this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite no-employment-right and no-equity clause, with an express "except as set forth in the Plan" carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 12.15 and with Section 4.5's anti-alienation rule.
judgments.clause_name: 12.16 Trust Grants No Interest to Employees

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite perpetual duration subject to the amendment and termination provisions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Accurately cross-references Article 10, which contains Sections 10.1-10.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short substitution amendment; it retitles 12.8(b) from "Fund Administrator" to "Fund Director" without explanation, and recites that "the Plan is hereby amended" when it in fact amends the Trust Agreement. That recital/operation mismatch is a mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.1 defines "Administrator" and Section 7.1 assigns duties to the Administrator, so introducing "Fund Director" creates a small terminological disconnect with the defined term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amended text adds "or such other interest rate that the Trustees deem appropriate given [the] circumstance," replacing a fixed rate with an unbounded discretionary alternative — the outer limit of that discretion is undefined. The OCR is also badly degraded at the operative words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.4(a) and 9.7(b)-(c) both compute amounts "in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5," which now yields either 18% or whatever the Trustees choose — leaving those cross-references indeterminate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite address substitution; the Association's address is truncated in the OCR but the operation is mechanical. It again uses "Fund Director" rather than the defined "Administrator."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Amendment No. 1 which it supersedes; the Director/Administrator label mismatch with Section 1.1 persists but is immaterial to notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A full replacement of the Preamble naming four current Trustees; definite, though the stray "2. the following:" line before the quoted text is an artifact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with amended Sections 3.1 and 3.3 naming the same four individuals, so it is internally consistent as amended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence reads "The appointment of Trustees shall be selected by the provisions of Section 3.4" — "selected" is plainly an error for "governed," a grammatical mistake in the operative sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Moving to a 2-2 board makes Section 6.3's quorum of two from each side require all four Trustees and makes Section 6.2(b)'s "any four Trustees" a unanimity requirement for calling special meetings — an incoherence introduced by this amendment.
judgments.clause_name: Amendment No. 4, 2. Section 3.1 Composition of Trustees

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of four named Trustees; nothing to construe beyond identification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with amended Sections 3.1 and the amended Preamble.
judgments.clause_name: Amendment No. 4, 3. Section 3.3 Selection of Trustees

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Still titled "Removal of Union Trustees" while the text prescribes who holds the office and addresses removal only by operation of law; the automatic-office rule leaves no route for the Union to remove a Trustee who remains in union office.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.10 gives the principal officer power to designate a successor "in which case a Successor Union Trustee shall be elected from the full-time officers of the Union," which does not sit easily with the amended 3.8's automatic incumbency rule.
judgments.clause_name: Amendment No. 4, 4. Section 3.8 Removal of Union Trustees
